main_body: Heart-shaped fern fronds in a half-round terracotta pot, drawn almost face-on
top_band: No real top surface. Dark brown rim at rows ~9-10, 1-2px thick, with the fern covering where the soil opening would be.
evidence: Reading down the middle column: green fronds (rows 1-8), a dark brown rim of about 2 rows, then the tan-to-brown pot body, which tapers like a bowl. The rim is too thin to read as a surface. No soil ellipse or interior is visible, because the fronds cover the opening. The pot body is a flat face-on wedge with no front-edge highlight and no eave shadow. The fern is a flat frontal fan. This is a rim-only front elevation, not a 3/4 object.

style.evidence: The fern has about 3-4 greens with a bright highlight blob, and the pot has about 3-4 browns. The outlines are tinted dark green and dark brown, which is good. The leaves are smooth, simple shapes with no leaf clumps or per-frond detail. The pot is large smooth fills with no grain, speckle or rim texture. Most tiles carry only 3-5 colours, against the rich foliage clumps and bark texture of the references. It looks thinner and flatter than the reference trees.
